## About the Author

**James Allen** — Data Science student at [New College of Florida](https://www.ncf.edu/). This project was built using **R**, **Quarto**, and the **tidyverse** to explore how physical ballpark dimensions, wall heights, and environmental factors shape home run rates across Major League Baseball.

## Data Sources

All ballpark and batted-ball data come from **[MLB Baseball Savant](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/)**. Stadium dimensions, fence heights, and annual park factor indices (2018–2026, where **100** represents the MLB average baseline—values above 100 favor hitters and values below 100 favor pitchers) are sourced from the [Statcast Park Factors Leaderboard](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/leaderboard/statcast-park-factors). Individual home run metrics—including exit velocity, launch angle, hit distance, pitch speed, and batter handedness splits—are collected from [Baseball Savant Statcast Search](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_search).
:::
